news.title: "Training stopped" is not a certificate. A policy can stall because it is stuck, out of gr…
news.author: artifocial
news.snippet: "Training stopped" is not a certificate. A policy can stall because it is stuck, out of gradient, or cycling too slowly to see. Equilibrium is a different claim: nobody can profitably deviate. Supervised learning descends a scalar loss. A game follows a vector field that is not the gradient of anything — so rotation is a failure mode single-loss training never has. Approximate exploitability is a lower bound — distrust the low numbers. https:// artifocial.com/blog/game-insid e-the-network-2026-aug-28 # GameTheory # MachineLearning

As part of my AI Engineering journey, I recently worked on a project that helped me unders…
news.author: hackaday@www.urbanmind.net
news.snippet: As part of my AI Engineering journey, I recently worked on a project that helped me understand how Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) works in practice. I built a Hybrid RAG system that combines FAISS vector search and BM25 keyword search to retrieve relevant information from a knowledge base and use it to generate grounded answers. In this post, I’ll briefly share what I built, how the system works, and some of the things I learned along the way. Why RAG? Large Language Models are great at generating natural-language responses, but they may not have access to information contained in a specific document or knowledge base. RAG addresses this by first retrieving relevant information from an external knowledge base and then providing that information to the LLM as context. The basic workflow is: User Query ↓ Retrieve Relevant Information ↓ Provide Context to LLM ↓ Generate Answer For my project, I wanted to take this a step further by combining semantic search and keyword search. 🔍 Hybrid Retrieval The system uses two retrieval methods: Vector Search with FAISS Document content is divided into smaller chunks and converted into vector embeddings. These embeddings are stored in a FAISS index, which is used to find documents that are semantically similar to the user’s query. This is useful even when the query and the document use different wording. Keyword Search with BM25 The second retrieval method is BM25. BM25 focuses on the occurrence and importance of terms in the query and documents. This makes it useful for exact terminology, technical terms, names, and identifiers. Instead of depending on only one retrieval method, both approaches are combined. User Query │ ┌──────────┴──────────┐ ↓ ↓ FAISS Search BM25 Search Semantic Search Keyword Search │ │ └──────────┬──────────┘ ↓ Hybrid Ranking ↓ Relevant Context ↓ LLM ↓ Final Answer The FAISS and BM25 scores are normalized and combined using weighted scoring. The results are then ranked, and the highest-ranked chunks are used as the final context. Document Chunking Before retrieval, the documents are divided into smaller chunks. Chunking is an important part of a RAG pipeline because the size of a chunk can affect retrieval quality. Very small chunks may lose important context, while very large chunks may contain unnecessary information and reduce retrieval precision. So the goal is to find a balance between context and retrieval accuracy. Each chunk is also stored with metadata such as its document ID and title, making it easier to identify the source of retrieved information. Adding Agentic RAG Another part of the project was exposing the retrieval system as a tool for an agent. I created a knowledge-base search tool: knowledge_base_search(query) The agent can use this tool to retrieve relevant information before generating the final response. The workflow becomes: User Query ↓ Agent ↓ knowledge_base_search() ↓ FAISS + BM25 ↓ Hybrid Ranking ↓ Retrieved Context ↓ LLM ↓ Final Answer The agent is instructed to use the retrieved information when answering questions and avoid generating unsupported information. If the knowledge base doesn’t contain sufficient information, the system can indicate that the information isn’t available. LLM For response generation, I used Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct through InferenceClientModel. The LLM doesn’t perform the initial retrieval. Instead, the retrieval tool provides relevant information to the agent, which is then used as context for generating the response. This separation between retrieval and generation helps keep the knowledge base as the primary source of information. Implementation The project was initially developed in Google Colab and later reorganized into a single executable Python application in VS Code. The main pipeline includes: Documents ↓ Chunking ↓ Embeddings ↓ FAISS Index + BM25 Index ↓ Hybrid Retrieval ↓ Ranking ↓ Agent Tool ↓ Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct ↓ Answer The embedding model and retrieval indexes are initialized when the application starts, so the complete retrieval pipeline doesn’t need to be rebuilt for every question. Testing I tested the system with questions related to the information available in the knowledge base. For example: Why is document chunking important in a RAG system? The hybrid retrieval system ranked the Document Chunking source highest because it directly addressed the question. The retrieved context was then passed to the agent and used to generate the final response. I also considered questions where the required information isn’t available in the knowledge base. In those cases, the system is designed to avoid simply falling back to the LLM’s general knowledge. What I Learned Working on this project helped me understand that building a RAG system isn’t just about connecting an LLM to a vector database. Several components have a direct impact on the quality of the final answer: Document chunking Embedding quality Retrieval strategy Keyword matching Hybrid ranking Context construction Agent behavior LLM generation One of the biggest takeaways for me was understanding the importance of the retrieval stage. Even a powerful LLM can produce a poor answer if the relevant information isn’t retrieved properly. What’s Next? There are several improvements I would like to explore next, including: Better chunking strategies Reranking retrieved documents Query rewriting Semantic chunking Improved relevance filtering Source citations Automated retrieval and answer evaluation Automatic optimization of hybrid retrieval weights These are some of the areas identified for future improvement in the current system. Conclusion This project gave me practical experience with Hybrid RAG, vector search, BM25, FAISS, embeddings, agentic tool use, and LLM-based generation. The key idea I took away is: Good RAG isn’t only about the LLM — the quality of the retrieved context matters just as much. By combining semantic and keyword-based retrieval, the system can use both the meaning of a query and its important exact terms before generating a response. This was a great learning experience, and I’m looking forward to exploring more areas of AI Engineering and RAG systems. 🚀 ⸻ Tech Stack Python · FAISS · BM25 · Sentence Embeddings · Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct · Agentic RAG · Vector Search · VS Code AI # RAG # ArtificialIntelligence # MachineLearning # LLM # Python # AgenticAI # FAISS # BM25 # ai # llm # rag # software # coding # development # engineering # inclusive # community Building a Hybrid RAG System with FAISS, BM25, and Agentic AI

tele.title: Comin Asia and Nokia build sovereign AI infrastructure across Southeast Asia
tele.snippet: AI-ready data centres planned for Cambodia and Laos; Nokia partnership for regional sovereign AI infrastructure.

tele.title: Huawei expands Vietnam footprint through energy, AI, and 5G partnerships
tele.snippet: Partnerships spanning digital energy, AI, telecom infrastructure and industrial digitalization in Vietnam.

tele.title: Cellcard doubles 5G footprint to 500+ sites, targets 1,000 by end-July
tele.snippet: Cellcard CSX-listed operator: 500+ 5G BTS deployed since Jan 2026 launch; accelerating toward 1,000 sites across Phnom Penh and central region.

tele.title: Huawei and ZTE strengthen presence in Vietnam with new 5G network deal wins
tele.snippet: Huawei consortium ~$23M 5G equipment contract; Viettel targeting 20,000 new 5G base stations in 2025. 11,000+ stations deployed nationwide.

tele.title: EU warns Vietnam: Chinese 5G vendors may deter foreign investment
tele.snippet: Ericsson and Nokia on core; Huawei and ZTE winning RAN/antenna contracts. EU Commissioner Sikela: 5G is the new battlefield for trusted vendors.

tele.title: Viettel targets 98% population 5G coverage; adds 20,000 sites in 2026
tele.title_orig: Viettel hướng tới phủ sóng 5G tới 98% dân số
tele.snippet: Deputy CEO Le Quang Hieu at MWC 2026: ~30,000 5G SA sites by end-2025; planning +20,000 in 2026 for 98% coverage.

tele.title: Vietnam eyes new 5G deals with Chinese tech firms despite US warnings
tele.snippet: Mobifone in talks with Huawei; Viettel and VNPT signed 5G supply contracts with ZTE and Huawei. Ericsson and Nokia still supply core network.

tele.title: Vietnam pursues new 5G deals with China despite US warnings
tele.title_orig: Việt Nam nhắm thỏa thuận 5G mới với Trung Quốc, bất chấp cảnh báo của Mỹ
tele.snippet: BBC Vietnamese: Mobifone negotiating with Huawei; Viettel/VNPT already signed with ZTE and Huawei for 5G equipment.

tele.title: Despite US warnings, Vietnam plans more 5G contracts with Chinese vendors
tele.title_orig: 不顾美国警告 越南拟与中企签更多5G网络合约
tele.snippet: Zaobao: Mobifone tender favors Chinese firms; Huawei 5G gear seen near US Consulate in HCMC; follows Viettel/VNPT ZTE/Huawei deals.

tele.title: Viettel to trial 6G in 2028 with Qualcomm strategic alliance
tele.title_orig: Viettel sẽ thử nghiệm 6G vào năm 2028
tele.snippet: MWC 2026: Viettel joins Qualcomm 6G alliance; commercial 6G target from 2029; co-develop premium AI smartphones.

tele.title: Cambodia 5G trial: Cellcard leads download speeds in early Ookla tests
tele.title_orig: អ៊ីនធើណិត 5G សាកល្បងជំហានដំបូងនៅកម្ពុជា
tele.snippet: AMS Khmer: Ookla trial shows Cellcard 548 Mbps, Smart 336 Mbps, Metfone 218 Mbps; 1,500+ 5G sites by March 2026.

tele.title: 1,500 5G base stations deployed in Cambodia's 5G race so far
tele.snippet: Smart Axiata 674, Metfone (Viettel) 531, Cellcard 289 stations. Ministry accelerating mobile and FWA rollout.

tele.title: Vietnam 5G median speed tops 500 Mbps for the first time; Viettel leads at 617 Mbps
tele.title_orig: Mạng 5G Việt Nam lần đầu vượt 500 Mbps
tele.snippet: VNNIC i-Speed Jan 2026: national 5G median 594.81 Mbps; Viettel 617 Mbps vs VNPT 311 Mbps and MobiFone 188 Mbps.

tele.title: Cambodia launches 5G as all three mobile operators switch on networks
tele.snippet: Cellcard, Metfone and Smart launched 5G from Jan 2026. Phased rollout from Phnom Penh and 14 provinces.

tele.title: Vietnam 5G mass deployment opens platform for app developers
tele.title_orig: 越南5G大规模部署：为应用程序开发搭建新平台
tele.snippet: VietnamPlus Chinese: Viettel 30,000 5G sites, 90% outdoor coverage; Huawei expert praises fast 5G e-commerce adoption.

tele.title: Huawei and ZTE win 5G contracts in Vietnam; Ericsson and Nokia retain core
tele.title_orig: 消息称华为中兴在越南斩获5G合同
tele.snippet: C114: Huawei $23M consortium deal; ZTE $20M+ antenna contracts; Nordic vendors on core; ~11,000 5G sites cover 26% population.
